A volunteer crew is needed for a transatlantic voyage on a 115-Foot Longship called the Draken Harald Hårfagre (Dragon Harald Fairhair) https://archive.today/ZGLSW/a12ecf2a6e5ce3031787bfb9bd50316295d180a5.png

The name honors an old Viking king, the first to unite Norway. At 115 feet this is the largest Viking ship ever built in modern times. Beam is 27 feet. She displaces 80 tons and carries 3,200 sq.ft. of sail. Longships like this were vessels of war.

This ship has been sea-trialed, and reportedly she has hit speeds of 14 knots.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6bTkmG5b-VQ

In May next year she will set out on a voyage from Norway to Newfoundland via Iceland and Greenland. You need at least two months of free time to do it and presumably should have some sort of useful skill to boost your chances of being selected. Conditions aboard look to be very Spartan by modern standards, with no shelter except for a tent on deck, but by traditional Viking standards it should be a veritable luxury cruise. The ship does have an engine, so you probably won’t have to do too much rowing, plus a modern stove and toilet. I’m also assuming you can wear modern clothing and foul-weather gear.
